headline: Bangladesh and China sign 13 MoUs to deepen cooperation across key areas
summary: The agreements were signed during Prime Minister Tarique's official visit to China, where he also met with President Xi Jinping.
details: Prime Minister Tarique's visit to China has resulted in the signing of 13 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) and two agreements to strengthen bilateral ties.
The cooperation will span various key sectors, aiming to deepen the strategic partnership between the two nations.
As part of the official visit, the Prime Minister met with Chinese President Xi Jinping to discuss mutual interests and regional stability.
The Prime Minister was received with a red-carpet welcome in China, highlighting the importance of the diplomatic engagement.
The agreements are expected to to facilitate growth in trade, infrastructure, and diplomatic cooperation between Bangladesh and China.
caption:
13 MoUs signed! Bangladesh and China strengthen their strategic partnership through a series of high-level agreements.

Prime Minister Tarique's visit to China has resulted in the signing of 13 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) and two agreements to strengthen bilateral ties.

The cooperation will span various key sectors, aiming to deepen the strategic partnership between the two nations.

As part of the official visit, the Prime Minister met with Chinese President Xi Jinping to discuss mutual interests and regional stability.

The Prime Minister was received with a red-carpet welcome in China, highlighting the importance of the diplomatic engagement.

The agreements are expected to to facilitate growth in trade, infrastructure, and diplomatic cooperation between Bangladesh and China.

headline_marked: Lone convict [[gets death penalty]] in Suranjit Sengupta grenade attack case
headline: Lone convict gets death penalty in Suranjit Sengupta grenade attack case
summary: A court has acquitted high-profile suspects including a minister and an MP, while sentencing one person to death for the 2004 attack.
details: The Sylhet Divisional Speedy Trial Tribunal has sentenced Hafiz Syed Naim Ahmed Arif, also known as Nimu, to death for his role in the attempted murder of former minister Suranjit Sengupta.
The court acquitted nine other suspects, including Expatriate Welfare Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury, ruling party whip GK Gouse, and MP Lutfozzaman Babar, finding the charges against them unproven.
The case dates back to a grenade attack on June 21, 2004, during a political rally in Derai Bazar, Sunamganj, where Suranjit Sengupta was addressing supporters.
While Suranjit Sengupta survived the attack, a Jubo League activist was killed and 29 others were injured in the blast.
Defence lawyer Borhan Uddin stated that charges were originally framed against 13 people, but only one was found guilty under three charges.
Following the verdict, Ariful Haque Choudhury and GK Gouse described the case as 'politically motivated' and expressed relief that the court acted independently based on evidence.
Lutfozzaman Babar claimed justice had prevailed after a long wait, alleging he had previously faced pressure to give false testimony in other grenade cases.
caption:
One man sentenced to death, nine others acquitted—including a minister and an MP—in a 20-year-old grenade attack case.

The Sylhet Divisional Speedy Trial Tribunal has sentenced Hafiz Syed Naim Ahmed Arif, also known as Nimu, to death for his role in the attempted murder of former minister Suranjit Sengupta.

The court acquitted nine other suspects, including Expatriate Welfare Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury, ruling party whip GK Gouse, and MP Lutfozzaman Babar, finding the charges against them unproven.

The case dates back to a grenade attack on June 21, 2004, during a political rally in Derai Bazar, Sunamganj, where Suranjit Sengupta was addressing supporters.

While Suranjit Sengupta survived the attack, a Jubo League activist was killed and 29 others were injured in the blast.

Defence lawyer Borhan Uddin stated that charges were originally framed against 13 people, but only one was found guilty under three charges.

Following the verdict, Ariful Haque Choudhury and GK Gouse described the case as 'politically motivated' and expressed relief that the court acted independently based on evidence.

Lutfozzaman Babar claimed justice had prevailed after a long wait, alleging he had previously faced pressure to give false testimony in other grenade cases.
